column7: a campaign revoke whose grant removal failed left the item stamped revoked while the grant was still live (false ISO 27001 A.5.18 / SOC 2 CC6.2-6.3 evidence) and un-retryable; claim + removal + audit now run in one transaction so a failed apply rolls the claim back

the fault-free instance of the same defect and the anti-drift guard: a last-project-admin guard REFUSAL (an ordinary expected outcome, no fault injection) also used to stamp the item revoked; it now leaves it pending, and the assertion fails if the access-review path ever stops reusing the public removal path lock+guard wrapper

the same rollback against real Postgres, which aborts a transaction on a failing statement rather than SQLites more forgiving semantics - a rollback path that works on SQLite is not evidence it works here

the lock-ordering review #2676 asked for: two reviewers on independent connections revoking different items that share one projectAdminGuardLockKey, each holding its own transaction, must both complete - pins named-lock-outside/transaction-inside and the two-pooled-connection budget (pgOpen MaxOpenConns(2)) a third connection inside the transaction would break
